questions.question: Operating combination vehicles usually requires ____ operating single vehicles.
questions.explanation: Combination vehicles are heavier and longer than single vehicles. They need more driving skill to operate safely.

questions.question: When pulling a trailer, the air supply control lever should be in ____ position.
questions.explanation: The air supply control should be in the "normal" position to safely pull a trailer. This is the correct setting for tractor protection controls.

questions.question: Bobtail tractors are ____ to stop than tractors pulling full semitrailers.
questions.explanation: A bobtail tractor is a tractor with no trailer attached. Bobtail tractors take longer to stop and are harder to control than loaded tractors.

questions.question: In a double or triple combination, the ____ trailer should be directly behind the cab.
questions.explanation: Place the heaviest trailer closest to the tractor. The lightest trailer should go in the back.

questions.question: When driving a vehicle with Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS), brakes should be applied:

options.text: The same way as in a vehicle without ABS.
While the vehicle is in neutral.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same way as in a vehicle without ABS.
questions.explanation: Use the same braking technique in an ABS vehicle as you would in a regular vehicle.

questions.question: What is a bobtail tractor?

options.text: A tractor with no trailer attached
A tractor that speeds above the limit

questions.correctAnswerText: A tractor with no trailer attached
questions.explanation: A bobtail tractor is a tractor without a trailer. Drivers must be careful because bobtail tractors are difficult to operate.

questions.question: The trailer hand valve should be used:

options.text: To check if the trailer and tractor are connected.

questions.explanation: The trailer hand valve (trolley valve) controls the trailer brakes. Use it only to test the brakes. Using it while driving can cause a skid.

questions.question: If you must cross traffic while driving a combination vehicle, you should:

options.text: Assume other drivers will make room for you.
Wait for a gap large enough for your vehicle to cross safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for a gap large enough for your vehicle to cross safely.
questions.explanation: Combination vehicles need more space than other vehicles. Always wait for a large enough gap in traffic before crossing.

questions.question: When braking with ABS, you should:

options.text: Push the brake pedal harder than normal.
Push the brake pedal as you normally would.
Push the brake pedal more lightly than normal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Push the brake pedal as you normally would.
questions.explanation: Brake in the same way with ABS as you would without ABS. Do not change your braking technique.

questions.question: If an air supply control is in "emergency" position:

options.text: The trailer emergency brakes will be applied.
The air supply to the trailer will increase.

questions.correctAnswerText: The trailer emergency brakes will be applied.
questions.explanation: When the air supply control is in "emergency" position, the air supply stops and the trailer emergency brakes apply.

questions.question: Keeping cargo centered on a truck can:
questions.explanation: A rollover happens more easily if cargo is loaded unevenly. Keep the load centered on the truck to prevent a dangerous rollover.

questions.question: Look into the back of the fifth wheel:

options.text: If your vehicle begins to skid.

questions.explanation: When inspecting a coupling, go under the trailer and look into the back of the fifth wheel. Make sure the fifth wheel jaws are locked around the kingpin.

questions.question: When testing ____, apply your vehicle's brakes with the hand control while moving forward slowly.
questions.explanation: To test the trailer service brakes, make sure the air pressure is normal and release the parking brake. Move forward slowly and apply the brakes with the hand control. If the brakes work, you will feel them activate.

questions.question: If a trailer begins to jackknife, the driver:

options.text: Should not apply the trailer hand brake.
Can straighten the trailer with the parking brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should not apply the trailer hand brake.
questions.explanation: If a trailer jackknifes, release the brakes so the trailer wheels regain traction. Do not apply the trailer hand brake because applying the brakes caused the wheels to lock in the first place.

questions.question: Pushing in the trailer air supply control will:
questions.explanation: Push in the trailer air supply control to send air to the trailer. Pull out the control to turn off the air supply and activate the emergency brakes.

questions.question: The best way to recognize that your trailer has started to skid is by:

options.text: Checking the trailer in your mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Checking the trailer in your mirrors.
questions.explanation: Watch your mirrors to see if your trailer jackknifes. This allows you to spot skidding as early as possible.

questions.question: A trolley valve:

options.text: Should only be used to test trailer brakes.
Should be used when parking uphill.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should only be used to test trailer brakes.
questions.explanation: The trailer hand valve (also called trolley valve or Johnson bar) controls the trailer brakes. Use it only for brake testing. Do not use it while driving because it can cause a skid. Do not use it when parking because it may release the brakes holding the vehicle.

questions.question: If the emergency air line loses pressure:

options.text: The tractor protection valve will close.
The rear trailer will detach from the combination.

questions.correctAnswerText: The tractor protection valve will close.
questions.explanation: The tractor protection valve keeps air in the trailer brakes if the trailer breaks away or leaks. When emergency line air pressure drops, the tractor protection valve closes and activates the emergency trailer brakes.

questions.question: The trailer hand valve should not be used while you are driving because:

options.text: It will disconnect from the vehicle.
You will stop the vehicle too quickly.

questions.explanation: Never use the trailer hand valve while driving. It can cause your trailer to skid.

questions.question: How much space should be between the upper and lower fifth wheel?

options.text: A maximum of two inches of space

questions.explanation: Before you drive, inspect all couplings. There should be no space between the upper and lower fifth wheel.
